messages:
Maya: quick note — ran the FAv3 integration on the nightly canary pool and hit a reproducible tail regression on paged-KV workloads. low-batch (1-2 reqs) 80-150 token tails are worse.
Raj: rough numbers?
Maya: short dump from profiler attached below (sanitized). core difference looks like scheduling overhead + more kernel launches for the same seq lengths when paged-KV is present.

```text
# flashv3 (canary, 8xA100, batch=1)
kernel: flashv3/paged
p50: 34ms
p90: 180ms
p95: 230ms
extra kernel launches: 3 per token

# flashv2 (prod, same hw)
kernel: flashv2/paged
p50: 28ms
p90: 150ms
p95: 185ms
extra kernel launches: 1 per token
```

Sara: ugh. Any chance this is a telemetry artifact (different batching config) or real kernel behavior?
Maya: repeated with fixed batcher config (force-batch-size=1) and still see delta. Also observed higher CPU on the scheduler threads during the tail.

Leo: could be matrix scheduling ordering in the FAv3 path — if it breaks contiguous kernel fusion we get extra launches. Did you capture per-kernel times + launch counts?
Maya: yes, logs show more micro-launches in the attentn fusion pipeline. I can paste a short trace snippet.

```text
trace: request=abc123
  kv-check: hit
  prepare-matrices: 0.6ms
  split-slices: 1.8ms
  kernel-launch-1: 0.4ms
  kernel-launch-2: 0.5ms
  kernel-launch-3: 0.6ms  # extra
  finalize: 0.7ms
```

Raj: ok. Hypothesis: FAv3 introduced per-slice safety path for paged-KV that disallows certain fused kernels when non-contiguous KV pages are present.
Maya: sounds plausible.

Sara: action items we should consider:
- add a short-lived feature flag to gate matrix-scheduler heuristics for paged-KV (fa_v3_matrix_gate)
- emit detailed telemetry for kernel-launch-count, fused-kernel-used boolean, and per-request seq_len/batch_size
- run a canary A/B comparing FAv2 vs FAv3 on single-request workloads and paged-KV heavy traces
- implement fallback: if per-request kernel-launch-count > threshold, fallback to flashv2 for that request

Leo: agree. Also add a smoke test that reproduces extra-launch pattern in CI using the small mocked paged-KV dataset.

Maya: sample telemetry event names I propose:
- runtime.attention.kernel.name = "flashv3"|"flashv2"
- runtime.attention.kernel.launch_count = int
- runtime.attention.fused = true|false
- runtime.attention.kv.paged = true|false
- runtime.attention.latency_ms = float

Raj: thresholds for automated fallback? I'd start with p95 latency delta > 1.2x vs baseline and launch_count >= 3 for batch_size <=2.

Maya: rollout plan draft:
- feature-flag off by default
- Stage 1 (dev): enable on nightly canaries for 24h with tracing; collect metrics
- Stage 2 (canary): enable on 5% of canary pool with A/B routing (flashv2 baseline)
- Stage 3 (gradual): enable 25% prod read-only for <= 72h measuring p50/p95 and failed-fallback rate
- Gates: if p95 increases > 15% or fallback rate > 2% stop rollout and auto-disable flag
- Quick rollback: infra-bot command `infra-bot disable-flag fa_v3_matrix_gate` to force immediate fallback

Sara: do we have a query for measuring the launch_count distribution? I can add a grafana panel.
Maya: `sum by (kernel) (rate(runtime_attention_kernel_launch_count[5m]))` plus a percentile panel for runtime.attention.latency_ms segmented by kernel/fused.

Leo: tests & perf harness:
- add microbench for paged-KV with varying seq_len [64,128,256] and batch_size [1,2,8]
- assert kernel-launch-count <= expected (baseline from FAv2)
- perf-regression CI job that fails on >10% p95 regression for batch_size<=2

Raj: ops concerns — we need to ensure fallback doesn't thrash. If many requests flip between kernels mid-request we could amplify tails. Fallback should be sticky per-request and use a short ttl for decisions.
Maya: agreed. fallback semantics: evaluate after prepare phase for that request; if condition met, switch to flashv2 for the remainder of the request only. Do not toggle back mid-request.

infra-bot: feature flag created: `fa_v3_matrix_gate` (default: false). Use `infra-bot enable-flag fa_v3_matrix_gate --env=canary --percent=5` to start.

Ops-bot: deploy-runner started canary job #3254 (flashv3-matrix-sweep). Logs at https://ci.example/reports/3254

Sara: I'll own the Grafana panels + alert: alert if p95_delta > 12% for more than 10 minutes or fallback_rate > 1% sustained for 5min.

Maya: I'll prepare the CI microbench and a repro harness with the trace that shows extra launches.

Raj: I'll add the kernel-launch-count telemetry and the fallback gating logic into the routing layer.

Leo: timeline? can we get a dev canary by EOD tomorrow?
Maya: yes, I can push a patch and a canary image tonight. ping me if you need the trace.

Sara: thanks. tagging this thread for followups and adding checklist to the PR.

Maya: summary checklist:
- [ ] telemetry: kernel_launch_count, fused_flag, kv_paged
- [ ] feature flag fa_v3_matrix_gate
- [ ] A/B canary job + grafana dashboards
- [ ] CI microbench + perf gate
- [ ] fallback-per-request implementation
- [ ] smoke test repro for paged-KV extra launches

Leo: perfect. I'll coordinate the smoke CI job and ensure we have an automated rollback hook.

Maya: :thumbsup: will post trace and PR link in this thread when ready.
